a: the fixture traverses identify, extract, patch, replay, snapshot, and evidence contracts, while capability reports exclude it from every real-engine and multi-title count.
m: A deterministic non-retail fixture engine exercises the adapter, patch, runtime, and conformance contracts without being counted as real engine support.

a: the common product path extracts, localizes, patches, executes, and renders two real RealLive titles with complete scoped-unit coverage and no title-specific mechanism.
m: RealLive, whose scene compression is repeatedly named AVG32, is intended to support real detection, whole-archive decode, structured extraction, byte-correct patchback, narrative structure, deterministic execution, and faithful audiovisual rendering.

a: two real Siglus titles with distinct profiles complete identify through rendered patched-byte observation with zero unknown in-profile operations.
m: Siglus/SiglusEngine is intended to support executable/key profiling, Scene and configuration containers, complete bytecode semantics, bridge production, patchback, runtime execution, and faithful rendering.

a: two real Softpal titles using distinct choice/container variants extract, patch, execute, and render through the registered product path.
m: Softpal/Sv20/Pal.dll is intended to support PAC and loose-file inputs, text and script decoding, choice semantics, byte-correct patchback, structure, and an executable runtime port.

a: two real NeXAS titles spanning distinct pack types extract and patch through the common adapter contract, and unsupported pack types fail with a typed capability diagnostic before writes.
m: NeXAS is intended to have a Kaifuu adapter covering the catalogue’s container and compression variants rather than a detector-only entry.

a: one MV and one MZ real title complete configured-scope extraction, localization, patchback, launch, and observed translated-output validation, including plugin text declared in their profiles.
m: RPG Maker MV/MZ is intended to cover JSON text, plugin-owned text, encrypted media, patch application, and browser or NW.js runtime observation.

a: two real RGSS3 titles with different archive/profile variants extract and patch supported text and produce a runtime observation through the generation-specific adapter.
m: RPG Maker VX Ace/RGSS3 is modelled as a separate generation with RGSSAD, Ruby Marshal, binary patching, and native/Wine runtime concerns.

a: a plain title and at least two differently encrypted real titles extract, patch, launch, and render without treating inline script as dialogue or exposing key material.
m: KiriKiri/KiriKiri Z combines KAG script semantics with plain and per-title encrypted XP3 containers, helper profiles, patchback, and a native or reimplemented runtime.

a: two real Ren’Py projects round-trip supported scripts and emit route, screen-text, and callback observations; compiled or protected variants take the declared typed path rather than being misidentified as plaintext.
m: Ren’Py is intended as a plaintext/decompiled-script adapter with menu/label preservation plus native and web observation instrumentation, with compiled inputs explicitly profiled or delegated.

a: two real Wolf titles with different protection profiles extract, patch, and emit linked runtime observations with no raw key or private-path disclosure.
m: Wolf RPG Editor/Udita is intended to cover archive/protection profiles, databases and common events, deterministic patching, and native or browser capture.

a: two real BGI/Ethornell titles with distinct bytecode/container variants extract and patch every supported text reference and replay the patched references without false-positive strings.
m: BGI/Ethornell, also described as Buriko General Interpreter, is intended to cover container/compression variants, header and no-header bytecode, string references, offset-safe patching, and replay linkage.

a: two real Majiro variants expose complete supported string inventories, rebuild deterministically after a translation, and reject an unknown variant before writing.
m: Majiro is intended to progress from profiled bytecode/string-slot inventory to a deterministic writer and verified patchback.

a: two real CatSystem2 variants extract typed string tables, rebuild after translation, and reject unsupported encodings or layouts before writing.
m: CatSystem2 is intended to progress from compiled-script and Shift-JIS string-table inventory to deterministic write and verified patchback.

a: two real TyranoScript projects round-trip dialogue, choices, labels, jumps, variables, comments, and supported tags and then expose patched text through browser observation.
m: TyranoScript is intended as an independent null-key/plaintext adapter with tag-safe extraction, patchback, browser instrumentation, and tag replay.

a: two real Unity projects using I2 tables extract and patch the declared tables and observe the target text at runtime; a non-I2 Unity surface fails as out of profile.
m: Unity I2 Localization is intended to expose stable table keys and metadata, patch supported table assets, and provide a runtime capture profile without implying all Unity text is covered.

a: two real Naninovel projects produce engine-specific identify, inventory, extract, patch, and runtime capability observations, with any unsupported leg named explicitly.
m: Unity/Naninovel is separately intended to have evidence-backed readiness and profile modelling rather than inheriting support from generic Unity or I2.

a: at least three workers add three distinct engine adapters at the same time and their changes merge without coordinating edits to a shared switch, shared schema fork, or engine-specific common-code path.
m: Independent workers can add engine families concurrently through adapters, registries, and data without editing shared engine-identity branches.

a: every adapter fixture resolves to a provenance record and license/private classification, and a guard rejects an unclassified or copyrighted public fixture.
m: Fixture provenance, licensing, private-corpus use, reference-implementation use, and clean-room boundaries are explicit for every adapter.

a: adapters for three structurally different families satisfy the same conformance suite, and omitting any declared operation makes the suite fail.
m: A common adapter contract separates identify, inventory, extract, patch, verify, delta, and limitation reporting.

a: three project inputs resolve to three different registered profiles without a hardcoded engine default, while an omitted or unknown engine is rejected at the boundary.
m: Engine/profile selection is registry-driven and records engine family, variant, source roots, extract profile, codec, key requirements, and capabilities.

a: a generated cross-surface check finds a one-to-one family identifier mapping and fails when a surface introduces an alias or unregistered spelling.
m: One canonical engine-family vocabulary is shared by manifests, APIs, projects, capability reports, and runtime ports.

a: a detector-only fixture cannot produce a positive extract or patch row, and a real extracted-and-patched corpus produces only the legs observed.
m: Capability reports distinguish identify, inventory, extract, patch, structure, runtime, render, helper-required, partial, and unsupported evidence without inflating one leg into another.

a: changing an adapter manifest changes the generated matrix, and a mismatch between matrix and executable adapter conformance fails the parity gate.
m: A machine-generated matrix exposes each engine/profile’s positive capabilities, boundaries, limitations, and proof class to the catalog and product.

a: no tuple can claim a downstream leg without matching executable evidence for every prerequisite dimension.
m: Claimed compatibility is expressed across engine, variant, container, crypto, codec, surface, patchback, profile, secret/helper requirement, runtime, and diagnostic dimensions.

a: a fresh run reproduces the declared result, while any raw key, retail text/bytes, screenshot, private path, filename, or helper dump makes bundle validation fail.
m: A public-safe bundle packages the exact support tuple, redistributable fixture, proof hashes, outcomes, and limitations needed to reproduce compatibility evidence.

a: mutation of a claimed profile’s parser or writer makes the claimed-support regression runner fail with an in-profile defect classification.
m: Once a profile is declared supported, failures inside that exact profile are compatibility defects rather than silently reclassified unsupported input.

a: two engines swap at least one layer independently while producing the common bridge and patch contracts, and an absent required layer yields a typed capability error before writes.
m: Container, crypto, compression/codec, script parsing, patch layout, and verification are composable layers with typed boundaries.

a: plain, encrypted, helper-required, protected, misleading-extension, and unknown fixtures produce distinct exact evidence sets and stable diagnostics.
m: Detection classifies archive, encryption, protection, key, helper, packed, and unknown signals from evidence rather than confidence-only guesses.

a: a profile missing a required fixture, key reference, helper proof, patch proof, or redaction declaration is rejected and cannot enter the readiness index.
m: Profiles are centrally validated before they can authorize extraction, patching, or public readiness claims.

a: key resolution completes a supported decrypt/patch run while scans of logs, reports, debug output, persisted rows, and dropped holders find no raw, hex, or base64 key representation.
m: Raw key material is represented only by local secret references and resolved through a controlled, zeroizing, redacting boundary.

a: an approved helper returns a structured secret reference within byte/time limits, while a wrong hash, oversized input, timeout, cancellation, or unapproved executable is rejected before execution or consumption.
m: Optional key/protection helpers are capability-described, hash-allowlisted, bounded, cancellable, and isolated from pure extraction and patch logic.

a: equivalent helper results from two transports validate identically, and neither transport can place a raw key, local executable path, or helper dump in a public artifact.
m: Native, Wine/Proton, and remote helper transports share the same redacted result contract without making a platform helper the parser.

a: the XP3, Wolf, Siglus, and future crypt paths compile only through the shared holder, and a guard fails on a public raw-key constructor, Clone, or byte-bearing Debug implementation.
m: All crypt modules use one non-cloneable, debug-redacting, zeroize-on-drop secret holder with a private raw constructor.

a: a by-id request materializes every declared archive entry into a scratch root outside the vault, rejects schema drift or unsafe paths, and leaves the vault byte-identical.
m: Private corpora resolve by stable catalog identity into read-only materialization, with schema compatibility, complete extraction checks, and disjoint scratch storage.

a: empty/malformed metadata, a database decode failure, or any identity mismatch produces a typed diagnostic, while a valid artifact accounts for every declared file.
m: Canonical work, release, platform, language, engine, artifact, and file identities are validated against embedded sidecars and repository facts without dropping malformed rows.

a: a supported archive materializes exactly its manifest, while each adversarial or incomplete case produces no success tree and never substitutes fixture bytes.
m: Archive realization refuses traversal, unsupported codecs, silent member skips, partial trees, missing declared files, and synthetic fallback.

a: a qualifying family completes real extraction with no process spawn and any helper/oracle use remains explicitly outside that claim.
m: Families that claim pure native extraction decode their supported archives, crypto, and scripts in-process without executing the original binary or an external extractor.

a: scanning a mixed local corpus produces engine/profile/count/hash metadata sufficient for selection while public output contains no absolute path, private filename, or text payload.
m: Local owned corpora can be inventoried into redacted sidecars without publishing paths or content.

a: attempted, skipped, succeeded, failed, cancelled, and unsupported outcomes reconcile to the plan, successful candidates become secret references, and public aggregates reveal no key, path, filename, or content.
m: Owned local corpora can execute a bounded plan of static, manual, known-key, native, or assisted discovery attempts and validate candidates without publishing secrets.

a: manifests for three different engines validate through their own input maps, and shared validation contains no engine-specific filenames or defaults.
m: Common content addressing and privacy wrap per-engine corpus discovery, fingerprint, extract, and optional structure checks.

a: bridge outputs from three engine families validate against the same strict core schema, retain their namespaced extensions, and reject extra or malformed fields.
m: Every engine emits one strict bridge model for stable units, source bytes/hashes, speakers, choices, assets, spans, evidence, and engine extensions.

a: two extractions of unchanged bytes produce byte-identical IDs, and every patch entry resolves exactly one extracted unit without random-ID or duplicate collisions.
m: Unit, bridge, scene, choice, and source-revision identities are deterministic across repeated extraction and shared by extract and patch.

a: unchanged bytes patch successfully, while a one-byte source mutation causes a stale-source failure before any target write.
m: Native source hashes and byte ranges bind every translation and patch to the exact extracted revision.

a: a mixed corpus yields the expected exact count per surface and emits no code, control table, or binary block as dialogue.
m: Dialogue, speakers, choices, interface text, image text, audio-associated text, control markup, code, and binary data are classified explicitly.

a: normalized records retain a reversible link to raw source evidence, and a populated-rate report distinguishes source-absent, extractor-missing, and implemented-but-empty fields.
m: Engine-native surfaces normalize into canonical bridge roles without discarding raw provenance or conflating absent data with unimplemented extraction.

a: extraction and patchback round-trip a corpus exercising every registered span kind byte-for-byte outside translated text, and an unknown or malformed protected construct fails visibly.
m: Engine grammars identify variables, controls, ruby, tags, interpolation, names, asset references, and out-of-band markup as typed spans.

a: deletion, duplication, corruption, overlap, or an unregistered span makes preflight fail; reordered-but-identical spans follow whichever ordering policy is explicitly selected and tested.
m: Source protected spans map to target spans by typed identity with exact cardinality and non-overlap checks.

a: two engines normalize their own control markup through registered policies, and a literal string resembling another engine’s marker is preserved.
m: The common exporter derives visible text from declared spans or an adapter hook rather than spelling an engine marker in shared code.

a: a Shift-JIS engine and a UTF-8 JSON engine both pass their correct policies through the same release gate, and applying the wrong policy fails.
m: Encoding, control grammar, choice constraints, byte and box budgets, and allowed runtime evidence are supplied by the selected adapter; semantic totality and source-hash gates stay universal.

a: every accepted target re-encodes under its policy and a single unencodable code point, noncanonical form, or over-budget slot fails before patching.
m: Text encoding, Unicode normalization, representability, byte budgets, and punctuation/width rules are explicit and deterministic.

a: a fixture with growing and shrinking strings rebuilds every referenced offset correctly, and overflow, invalid range, or mid-element target yields a typed error.
m: Shared primitives model byte spans, source-to-target offsets, string slots, instruction framing, references, and relocations without lossy narrowing.

a: injecting one failure in each category leaves the target untouched and returns the category-specific diagnostic.
m: Patch preflight validates coverage, source hashes, protected spans, encoding, assets, destinations, and capability boundaries before opening a write transaction.

a: failure injected after each staged write leaves either the previous complete output or the new complete output, never a mixed or partially promoted tree.
m: Patch staging, promotion, rollback, collision handling, and no-clobber semantics are atomic across multi-file outputs.

a: filesystem tracing on a large source shows no read/write proportional to unrelated files and hashes every untouched source file identically.
m: Patch application writes only changed archives/files and required manifest output rather than cloning an unrelated game tree.

a: a clean source plus delta reproduces the expected target hashes, while the wrong source revision, path collision, unsafe path, or missing asset is rejected.
m: A portable `.kaifuu` delta contains typed edits, assets, provenance, source constraints, manifest hashes, and verification receipts.

a: default patch production refuses incomplete configured scope; an explicit preview produces a manifest visibly marked partial and cannot pass release validation.
m: Partial extraction or translation cannot masquerade as a complete release patch, although an explicit preview path can be recorded.

a: a mixed patch changes only containers/scenes with a genuine target edit and hashes every untouched byte range identically.
m: Units whose visible target equals source do not trigger archive recompression or unrelated byte changes.

a: malicious path, symlink, hard-alias, and dot-segment fixtures are all rejected before writes, while valid nested paths remain inside the selected target root.
m: Relative paths, canonical roots, no-follow writes, nested symlinks, dot segments, aliases, traversal, and vault/scratch separation are enforced uniformly.

a: a corpus containing dialogue, interface, image, audio, and opaque assets produces an exact inventory whose unhandled items carry typed limitations.
m: Text-bearing and non-text assets are inventoried with kind, hash, metadata, translation policy, and patchability rather than being silently omitted.

a: a known image fixture yields the expected regions and source text, and a changed image hash invalidates the OCR mapping.
m: Image text can be detected into bounded regions with OCR evidence and mapped back to patchable assets.

a: a supported image and audio replacement are observed in the patched build, and every asset outside the selected scope remains byte-identical.
m: Configured image and encrypted-media replacements decrypt or decode, replace, re-encode or re-encrypt, patch, and verify without altering excluded assets.

a: RealLive and two non-RealLive requests round-trip through the same endpoint with adapter-owned fields, while an omitted engine or foreign field is rejected.
m: CLI, API, Studio, and internal extract requests are required discriminated unions derived from registered adapter capabilities.

a: the command emits every in-scope unit exactly once from a real archive and its output feeds the whole-project localizer without a manual conversion.
m: A shipped user path can extract a whole configured project into one bridge plus structure input, not only one scene/unit.

a: a RealLive and a non-RealLive provider each produce valid scene/route/choice/character graphs consumed by the same downstream snapshot builder.
m: Per-engine structure providers emit a common graph with opaque stable IDs plus namespaced native evidence.

a: a multi-work archive resolves at least two roots, enumerates disjoint scoped units, inherits shared context, and supports an explicit entry override when automatic discovery cannot decide.
m: One archive can be carved into multiple works from decoded structure and operator entry metadata, with shared super-scope context and per-work overrides.

a: a scanner finds no named-title mechanism or title-derived constant in production source, and a new title in an existing family runs by adding data only.
m: Game/title identity, paths, dimensions, compiler versions, opcode aliases, fixture labels, and corpus counts live in registries, manifests, or test data rather than shipped mechanisms.

a: two differently laid-out real titles resolve the correct data root and profile, while a lookalike directory is rejected.
m: RealLive detection recognizes real nested and flat layouts, configuration, archive signatures, compiler/profile evidence, and declared screen settings.

a: all populated scenes of two real archives partition the file without overlap, underflow, or trailing unaccounted bytes.
m: The fixed scene directory, typed scene header, populated slots, offsets, and archive bounds are parsed exactly.

a: round-trip and differential tests produce byte-identical decompressed content for every corpus scene and fail on a one-bit codec mutation.
m: AVG32 compression/decompression, XOR mask, framing, and independent Kaifuu/Utsushi implementations agree on real and edge-case streams.

a: encrypted and plaintext real profiles both decode cleanly; forced recovery failure returns a typed error rather than ciphertext/mojibake output.
m: Eligible second-level encrypted scenes are recovered through a no-key-leak boundary and staged consistently for extraction, patch, and runtime.

a: all scenes in two real corpora re-emit byte-identically from the framing manifest and a truncated or adversarial expression yields a typed bounded error.
m: Every expression piece, store/memory reference, argument boundary, special parameter, select block, and goto pointer is parsed without recursion, desynchronization, or fabricated defaults.

a: two complete real archives contain zero generic or unknown operations under an exact known-opcode set, and an invented opcode inside a known module is rejected.
m: Commands are recognized per operation, not merely bucketed by module, with raw tuple preserved and oracle-checked sub-identity.

a: two real configurations populate every declared supported field, malformed numerics fail explicitly, and noncontiguous namespace keys past a gap are retained.
m: Configuration namespaces, compiler-version module lattice, screen size, syscalls, routes, names, archive declarations, and malformed values are typed without silent drops.

a: a full scan of two real archives emits zero binary/control-table units and retains every known dialogue-bearing command argument.
m: Only semantically typed dialogue/name/choice text becomes translatable units; kidoku tables, command blobs, binary Shift-JIS runs, and system data do not.

a: per-field population over two titles matches source evidence, known speakers are not labelled unknown, and unresolved identity is explicit rather than guessed.
m: Raw speaker text, display identity, safe label, canonical identity, reveal state, color, and voice linkage remain distinct and evidence-backed.

a: mixed prose plus markup from two corpora extracts as visible text plus protected spans and patches back byte-correctly.
m: Speaker delimiters, font/color/face tags, interpolation, ruby, and engine-level markup are recognized from documented grammar rather than title literals.

a: each modality yields exact option/target mappings and no option index shifts when arguments include non-text values.
m: Text, spatial, graphical, button-object, and interpolation-bearing choice forms expose labels, branch targets, geometry/art references, and protected expressions.

a: translated multi-option real choices re-decode with identical target topology, while dialogue-only scope leaves every choice byte-identical.
m: Configured choice translation is NextString-safe and updates framing and branch structure without touching excluded choices.

a: length-changing patches on two real titles reparse with the same scene topology, zero new unknown operations, and correct post-edit jump destinations.
m: Rebuilding supports longer and shorter target text by rewriting scene offsets and recalculating internal and cross-control-flow targets.

a: a patch keyed solely from a fresh extract applies through the adapter without conversion, random-ID mismatch, or a parallel legacy path.
m: Extraction and patching share the same header, decompression, bridge producer, deterministic IDs, and scope semantics.

a: trusted-oracle or image-coherence comparison passes every supported type across two titles, including large backgrounds, and corrupt dimensions fail without allocation or arithmetic panic.
m: G00 image types and their compression variants decode coherently, completely, and safely rather than merely reaching a byte count.

a: real audio emits reproducible decoded events and save/load round-trips profile data for two titles without a title-named compiler default.
m: NWA/OVK audio and AVG-derived save/read formats are typed, bounded, and profile-driven.

a: two real titles are detected with the correct variant and a synthetic-magic-only detector fails the test.
m: Detection uses real Scene, configuration, and executable structure instead of fixture magic.

a: the chosen path yields a hash-addressed readable tree for two owned titles without modifying source media or publishing content.
m: Protected distributions can be lawfully materialized into a plaintext working tree or routed to a documented acquisition/profile boundary.

a: two real profiles decrypt with verified keys while wrong-key and unsupported-packer cases fail without exposing candidates.
m: The second-layer key is recovered or resolved from executable evidence into a secret reference and verified against the encrypted configuration.

a: every declared scene in two real containers extracts and re-encodes with exact table integrity.
m: The Scene container index, XOR, compression, scene list, string and label tables, and bounds are decoded deterministically.

a: two real configurations populate their expected records and a missing or malformed table fails explicitly.
m: The encrypted configuration yields names, speakers, settings, and other typed evidence required by extraction and runtime.

a: every scene across two real titles has zero unknown operations and full expression consumption, including variable-length system calls.
m: Expression stack, scope tags, text, flow, assignment, arithmetic, system-function calls, choices, and unknown detection are complete.

a: two title profiles with the same or differing maps decode all choices through the declared rule and an unregistered syscall does not become a choice.
m: Choice syscall identification comes from a documented engine ABI or per-profile schema, never a title-specific magic number.

a: every translatable string in two real corpora maps exactly once to a bridge unit and back to its native slot.
m: Dialogue, choices, speakers, protected spans, structure links, and source hashes emit the common bridge.

a: length-changing target text applies on two real titles, the patched containers decompile to the expected bridge, and a stale source is rejected.
m: Patchback rewrites strings/containers with stale-source protection, re-decompile self-check, and portable delta output.

a: one MV and one MZ real corpus round-trip every declared surface with exact source IDs and no excluded JSON mutation.
m: Maps, common events, database, system, terms, and declared JSON surfaces extract and patch as stable typed units.

a: the registered common plugin set emits all declared translatable parameters on two titles and the generic/deferred bucket is empty or an exact justified set.
m: Plugin-owned dialogue/UI text is extracted only through authored semantic profiles for common plugin families, with exact unsupported findings otherwise.

a: all commands in two real projects are recognized or belong to an exact opaque allowlist, and malformed codes produce typed diagnostics.
m: Event and script commands are typed rather than silently skipped or coerced on malformed command codes.

a: supported image and real audio signatures round-trip on one MV and one MZ title; a wrong key or unsupported signature stops before writes.
m: Encrypted suffix detection, key validation, image/audio decrypt, replacement, re-encrypt, and verification cover real MV/MZ media variants.

a: applying one delta to a clean real project changes only configured text/media and the patched project launches successfully.
m: JSON and media changes compose into the common patch and delta producer.

a: two distinct real RGSS3 profiles extract and patch declared text and reject an unsupported Marshal/archive variant before writing.
m: RGSSAD, Ruby Marshal, layered transforms, strings, and binary references have a profiled extract/patch path.

a: two real scripts round-trip all declared constructs and an iscript block contributes zero dialogue units.
m: KAG parsing preserves labels, macros, storage, speakers, choices, commands, page boundaries, and TJS-lite semantics while excluding inline script blocks from translation.

a: two real plain archives rebuild after target edits with identical untouched members and safe normalized paths.
m: Plain XP3 inventories, extracts, deterministically rebuilds, and verifies member paths, offsets, compression, and metadata.

a: at least two differently encrypted real titles decrypt, extract, patch, rebuild, and launch, while a self-authored fixture cannot satisfy the claim.
m: Per-title cxdec-profiled and TVP/helper crypt families resolve through explicit profiles rather than a fixture XOR scheme.

a: adversarial members for each case leave the target absent and return the exact expected error.
m: XP3 writing rejects UTF-16 path overflow, traversal, symlink materialization, unsupported flags, and layout inconsistencies before encoding.

a: each case produces its stable non-secret reason and no safe remediation text is replaced by blanket redaction.
m: Helper-required, missing-key, protected-executable, wrong-key, and out-of-profile outcomes remain distinct and human-readable after redaction.

a: the same script content in loose and packed form yields semantically identical bridge units and target output.
m: Plain KAG and XP3-backed KAG share bridge identities and patch semantics.

a: two real profiles enumerate every text-bearing database/script record and a mismatched profile fails before decode.
m: Wolf fingerprints, archive/protection variants, helper/key requirements, databases, and scripts are explicitly profiled.

a: two real variants launch with changed target text and scans find no key or private content in artifacts.
m: Supported encrypted archives decrypt, patch text-bearing data, rebuild safely, and verify through zeroizing keys.

m: Common-event and database relationships emit structure and bridge links useful to replay and context.

m: BGI container/compression, header and no-header bytecode variants, and string-reference tables are profile-driven.

m: BGI target changes rewrite affected references and remain loadable.

a: two real container variants produce the same unit inventory as their verified loose sources, or an unsupported transform is disclosed in the capability receipt.

m: TEXT data decrypt/encrypt and record-pool parsing are flag- and structure-driven.

m: SCRIPT disassembly uses an arity-driven stack-machine walk for text, speaker, select, pointers, and control flow.

a: both known label variants decode and patch correctly with no game/profile ID supplied to the strategy.
m: Immediate and decoupled SELECT labels are inferred from bytecode structure rather than build identity or magic values.

a: the observed call set across two titles maps to typed operations with no unexplained in-profile target.
m: Pal.dll call categories/functions are named sufficiently to recover flow, state, graphics, audio, and system effects.

m: Text rebuild, script repoint, and the real engine’s accepted override or repack mechanism produce a playable target.

m: Majiro bytecode string references, encodings, slots, deterministic rebuild, and unsupported variants are explicit.
